content: 1. Off Z, Zang OR, Kingue S, Djienouassi S, Kouontchou C, and colleagues conducted a discrete choice experiment to address the challenges of health workforce distribution in Cameroon. Their study aimed to develop strategies to improve the retention of healthcare workers in rural areas. This research was published in the International Journal of Health Policy and Management. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued guidelines on the development, attraction, recruitment, and retention of health workers in rural and remote areas. These guidelines are critical for addressing workforce shortages in underserved regions. 3. Abdel-All M, Angell B, Jan S, Howell M, Howard K, Abimbola S, and colleagues explored the preferences of community health workers in India through a discrete choice experiment. Their findings focused on the needs and desires of Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) and were published in BMJ Global Health. 4. Mandeville KL, Lagarde M, and Hanson K conducted a systematic review on the use of discrete choice experiments to inform health workforce policy. Their work, published in BMC Health Services Research, highlights the utility of this method in shaping effective workforce strategies. 5. Bowen DJ, Kreuter M, Spring B, Cofta-Woerpel L, Linnan L, Weiner D, and colleagues discussed the design of feasibility studies in healthcare research. Their work, published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine, provides a framework for conducting such studies effectively. 6. Dal Poz M, Gupta N, Quain E, and Soucat A edited a comprehensive handbook on monitoring and evaluating human resources for health. This resource is particularly tailored for application in lowand middle-income countries, offering practical tools for workforce assessment. 7. Buchan J reviewed the benefits of health workforce stability, emphasizing its importance for healthcare systems. This review was published in Human Resources for Health and provides insights into the value of retaining a stable health workforce. 8. Lewin S, Booth A, Glenton C, Munthe-Kaas H, Rashidian A, Wainwright M, and colleagues introduced the application of the GRADE-CERQual approach to qualitative evidence synthesis findings. Their work, published in Implementation Science, serves as an introduction to a series on this methodology.
